name: Grilled Steak & Onion Salad with Spicy Jalapeño-Pineapple Salsa

cookwares.name: grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ small pineapples
1 ½ jalapeño peppers
1 small bunch cilantro
1 ½ limes
3 heads butter (Boston) lettuce

instructions.primary_message: Cut skin off pineapples; quarter, core, and slice into ½-inch thick planks. Transfer to a large bowl.
Peel, halve, and slice onions into half-moons; add to the bowl with the pineapple. Drizzle with oil and toss to coat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ medium red onions
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the pan is hot, working in batches if necessary, add pineapple and onions. Grill, turning once, until charred and tender, about 4 minutes; remove to a large plate. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; place in the reserved bowl.

Quarter jalapeño peppers lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl with the garlic. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Juice limes into the bowl, then add oil, vinegar, honey, and salt; whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil
2 tbsp apple cider vinegar
1 tbsp honey
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Transfer the grilled pineapple to a cutting board and roughly chop. Add to the bowl with the dressing, stir to combine the salsa, and set aside.
Return grill pan to medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on another plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg striploin (New York strip) steak
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the pan is hot, coat with oil; working in batches if necessary, add steak to the pan and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to the plate with the onions and let rest, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop or tear the lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide lettuce between plates or bowls; top with steak, onions, and pineapple salsa. Enjoy!
